questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $3\times5$ matrix with row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$, null space $\operatorname{Null}(A)$, column space $\operatorname{Col}(A)$ and the null space $\operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})$ of $A^{\top}$. In which spaces do these four subspaces lie?
options: All four lie in $\mathbb{R}^5$, the larger of the two spaces

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix. Why is every $\boldsymbol{x}\in \operatorname{Null}(A)$ orthogonal to the row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$?
options: Each column of $A$ has dot product $0$ with $\boldsymbol{x}$
The rows of $A$ are orthonormal, so they are perpendicular
$\operatorname{Null}(A)$ is contained in the column space $\operatorname{Col}(A)$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix of rank $r$. Why does the null space of $A^{\top}$ satisfy $\dim \operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})=m-r$?
options: Rank–nullity for $A$ itself, which has $n$ columns
Rank–nullity for the $n\times m$ matrix $A^{\top}$, which has rank $r$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix, and split $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ as $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{x}_r+\boldsymbol{x}_n$ with $\boldsymbol{x}_r\in \operatorname{Row}(A)$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_n\in \operatorname{Null}(A)$. Which identity holds?
For a real $m\times n$ matrix $A$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$, which condition is equivalent to the solvability of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$?
A real $4\times6$ matrix $A$ has rank $3$. What are $\dim \operatorname{Row}(A)$, $\dim \operatorname{Null}(A)$, $\dim \operatorname{Col}(A)$ and $\dim \operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})$, in this order?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\\3&6\end{pmatrix}$, which of its four fundamental subspaces contains the vector $(-3,0,1)^{\top}$?

For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\\3&6\end{pmatrix}$, $\operatorname{Row}(A)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,2)^{\top}\}$ and $\operatorname{Null}(A)=\operatorname{span}\{(-2,1)^{\top}\}$. Writing $\boldsymbol{x}=(5,0)^{\top}=\boldsymbol{x}_r+\boldsymbol{x}_n$ with $\boldsymbol{x}_r\in \operatorname{Row}(A)$, $\boldsymbol{x}_n\in \operatorname{Null}(A)$, what is $\boldsymbol{x}_r$?

The matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ has rank $2$ and $\operatorname{Null}(A)=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$. What follows for $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ with $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^3$?
options: Every $\boldsymbol{b}$ gives a solution, since the columns are independent
Every $\boldsymbol{b}$ gives infinitely many solutions, since $m>n$
Every $\boldsymbol{b}$ gives exactly one solution, since $\operatorname{Null}(A)=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix and $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $A^{\top}A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$. Which argument shows $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$, giving $\operatorname{Null}(A^{\top}A)=\operatorname{Null}(A)$?
options: Multiply by $(A^{\top})^{-1}$ to cancel $A^{\top}$ from both sides
$A^{\top}A$ is square and symmetric, so its null space is $\operatorname{Null}(A)$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix. Why do the row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ and null space $\operatorname{Null}(A)$ meet only in $\boldsymbol{0}$?
options: They lie in different spaces, so they cannot share a vector
Their dimensions $r$ and $n-r$ never add up to more than $n$
$\operatorname{Null}(A)=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ whenever $A\neq O$, so nothing else is shared
A shared $\boldsymbol{x}$ is orthogonal to itself: $\boldsymbol{x}\cdot\boldsymbol{x}=0$

questions.question: A real $7\times4$ matrix $A$ has $\dim\operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})=5$. What is $\dim \operatorname{Null}(A)$?
A real $5\times3$ matrix $A$ has rank $2$. What is the dimension of the null space of the $3\times3$ matrix $A^{\top}A$?
A real $3\times3$ matrix $A$ of rank $2$ has row space $\operatorname{span}\{(1,1,0)^{\top},(0,1,1)^{\top}\}$. Which vector spans $\operatorname{Null}(A)$?
Let $A$ be a real square $n\times n$ matrix of rank $r$. How are its row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ and column space $\operatorname{Col}(A)$ related in general?
options: They are always equal, since $A$ is square
Both have dimension $r$, but they need not be equal
They are orthogonal complements of each other
Their dimensions differ unless $A$ is symmetric

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real square $n\times n$ matrix. Are $\operatorname{Null}(A)$ and $\operatorname{Col}(A)$, both subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$, always orthogonal to each other?
options: Yes: their dimensions $n-r$ and $r$ add up to $n$
No: they lie in different spaces, so orthogonality is undefined

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix with $\operatorname{Null}(A)\neq\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, and let $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ be solvable. How many solutions lie in the row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$?
options: Exactly one, whatever the dimension of $\operatorname{Null}(A)$
Exactly $r$, one per row-space basis vector

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\\3&6\end{pmatrix}$, $\operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})$ is spanned by $\boldsymbol{y}_1=(-2,1,0)^{\top}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}_2=(-3,0,1)^{\top}$. Is $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ solvable for $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,2,4)^{\top}$?
options: Yes, since $\boldsymbol{b}$ has no zero entry
